project.name: Sylphx Testing Playbook
project.summary: Sylphx Testing Playbook is a reusable documentation and template catalog for modern software testing methods, selection guides, and case studies.
goals: Maintain the testing-method taxonomy, maturity matrix, selection guide, templates, language notes, and case study.
Keep testing guidance reusable across repositories rather than product-specific.
Keep drift-prone tool and benchmark claims evidence-backed and reviewable.
nonGoals: Own individual product repositories' CI pipelines, fixtures, or production quality proof.
Replace enterprise engineering doctrine or repository-specific project manifests.
Present speculative tools, benchmarks, or current ecosystem claims without supporting evidence.

owns.name: testing-method-playbook
owns.description: Reusable testing method descriptions, ranking, selection guidance, language notes, templates, and case-study documentation.

doesNotOwn: Concrete test suites, CI policies, and production proof in consuming repositories.
Enterprise doctrine, org-wide rulesets, or reusable workflow implementation.
Vendor roadmaps or external tool maintenance state.
forbiddenCouplings: Do not make one product repository's local testing workflow the default for all consumers.
Do not encode enterprise policy here when the decision belongs in SylphxAI/doctrine.
Do not state current tool maturity, maintenance, or benchmark facts without evidence when those facts can drift.

delivery.deployPath: No hosted deploy path is declared. Default-branch documentation is the published source of truth.
delivery.productionProof: Markdown lint and internal link check pass, followed by default-branch readback for changed documentation.

commercial.decisionHome: not-applicable: reusable documentation and template catalog
commercial.metricsSourceOfTruth: repository traffic/adoption in consuming repos if later measured
guardrails: Commercial packaging or pricing decisions belong in consuming products or a future explicit commercial ADR.

gaps.description: Repository uses a legacy docs CI workflow and has not adopted ADR-29 admission fan-in contexts.
